chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Suleyman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) would not eat food nor drink a drink except that he said: 'O Allah, bless us in it and replace it with something better than it,' except for milk, for he would say: 'O Allah, bless us in it and increase us from it.'
ai.seo_question: What were the specific supplications recited by the Prophet before and after eating and drinking?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on dairy, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s distinct supplicatory practice, reflecting the Shia emphasis on specific prophetic traditions (sunan) in daily rituals. While general sustenance invokes a request for divine substitution and improvement, milk receives a unique prayer for continued abundance, underscoring its nutritional and spiritual significance in Islamic tradition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Al Rabie Bin Muhammad al Musly, from Abdullah Bin Suleyman, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said: ‘It never happened that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> would eat food nor drink a drink except that he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Change it for that which is better than it’, except for the milk, for he<sup>saww</sup> was saying: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Bless for us in it, and Increase it for us from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-Rabi’ ibn Muhammad al-Musliy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sulayman who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has stated this Hadith.

‘Whenever the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, ate food or drank a drink, he said, “O Lord, grant us blessing in it and better to replace it.” However when drinking milk he (the Messenger of Allah) would say, ‘O Lord, grant us blessing in it and increase it for us.’”
